transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marta Sosa (Horizon IQ Head of ML), Derek Lin (Platform Eng), Anita Chow (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick renewal/checkpoint, discuss capacity top-up, EU on-prem pilot requirements, security docs; agree next steps to run benchmarks and update contract amendment.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, um thanks for jumping on, i'm Jordan with Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marta: hey Jordan, doing good, thanks. we, uh, wanted to make sure we aligned on the renewal window and the eu on-prem pilot we've been chatting about.
[00:12] Derek: yeah hi all, quick note i have to duck around 40 minutes in but should be fine for most of this.
[00:17] Priya: great thanks derek, i'll try to focus the infra q's earlier. quick run, is the goal here to top up the retainer and spin the eu on-prem pilot before q3?
[00:25] Marta: yes that's the ask. we have two things: 1) add a 40% capacity buffer to our existing dedicated pool and 2) a short on-prem pilot in eu-west with a private control plane.
[00:35] Jordan: got it, so top-up + private pilot. for the top-up we generally have two paths: immediate monthly ramp on Dedicated versus reserving capacity for the pilot to use later. given your traffic, which are you leaning to?
[00:47] Derek: i think immediate. our QPS has a fairly spiky pattern and we want predictable throughput; reserving later makes the adoption timeline messy.
[00:54] Marta: predictable is the key word, yes. Also we discussed a hard latency SLO — 95th p99 token latency under our median seq length of ~512 — is that something you can commit to in the eu on-prem pilot?
[01:07] Priya: we can target 95th percentile token latency under that profile; we'll need the sample traffic and detailed seq-length histogram to lock the kernel/quantization settings. if you give us the profile, we can run a 48-hour benchmark with your payload.
[01:20] Derek: okay i'll export sample traces. there may be some PII in a subset; we'll mark those flows as sensitive.
[01:25] Marta: right, and about the private control plane — we need KMS integration with our HSM, SSO via SAML, and audit logs delivered to our SIEM. can Redwood support that out of the box or is there work on our side?
[01:37] Priya: we support customer KMS integrations and SAML SSO for private deployments; the audit logs can stream to a syslog or S3-compatible bucket. for HSM we typically integrate via your KMS provider; there might be a small connector to configure. i'll include the exact steps in the pilot checklist.
[01:52] Anita: procurement question — if we extend the term now, can we lock a fixed price for the new capacity for 12 months, and what's the cancellation/fallback if the on-prem pilot doesn't meet performance?
[02:03] Jordan: good question. we can do a 12-month amendment with a fixed rate for the added capacity. for fallback, typical language is that if pilot fails to meet agreed SLOs, you can roll the capacity back or use a credit towards Hosted usage for up to X months. i'll draft sample PO wording.
[02:17] Marta: sounds reasonable. one more security ask — SOC 2 report and penetration test summary, we've already asked, but we need them attached to the amendment for our infosec review.
[02:26] Jordan: yes we'll attach the SOC2 report and a redacted pentest summary. Priya can also share architecture notes for the private control plane.
[02:34] Priya: quick clarifying q on the pilot: do you plan to run the pilot with real traffic or synthetics? there's a difference for seeding the kv cache and for cold-start behavior.
[02:44] Derek: we prefer a mixed approach — real traffic for representative latency and synthetic for stress tests at peak QPS. also, we need ability to simulate regional failover, i.e., if eu-onprem is overloaded, fallback to hosted EU model.
[02:56] Priya: fallback routing is supported — policy-based routing can send to a hosted variant with a slightly lower throughput profile. we log the fallbacks, and those events can feed into your observability dashboards.
[03:06] Marta: on contract duration: our legal wants a rolling clause that allows us to increase capacity with 30 days' notice but only decrease at renewal periods. is that typical?
[03:16] Jordan: we've seen that pattern. we can include a capacity adjustment clause with a 30-day notice for increases and quarterly windows for decreases. i'll flag legal to add that language into the amendment.
[03:26] Anita: timeline wise, procurement needs the final pricing and PO draft 10 business days before our current term end, which is 2027-06-15. so, ideally, we need the amendment by 2027-06-01.
[03:37] Jordan: understood. our internal finance approval for a top-up of this size typically takes 3 business days after we send the amendment. Priya: anything else on the technical prerequisites?
[03:46] Priya: yes i need the k8s/flavor of your on-prem infra, networking egress details, and the HSM vendor. also, any compliance constraints for log retention in EU?
[03:56] Derek: we'll compile an infra doc — currently it's on-prem VMware with a small k8s cluster managed by platform. HSM is Thales. Log retention must stay in eu for 3 years for certain flows.
[04:07] Priya: ok that helps. for the benchmark, we'll need a VPN or direct connect to test from our runners into your environment; derek, is that something you can set up?
[04:16] Derek: yes we can do a temporary peering or a vpn; i'll coordinate with infra ops, but need to know the IP ranges and shorthand on the ports.
[04:23] Jordan: we'll include a checklist: IP ranges, ports, k8s node counts, KMS endpoint, SAML metadata, sample traffic, and compliance constraints.
[04:31] Marta: about pricing — can you run two numbers: (A) add 40% capacity to dedicated with a 12-month fixed rate and (B) a smaller top-up plus pilot fees for on-prem activation then commit afterwards? we need both to present to finance.
[04:43] Jordan: yes we can provide both options. option B will include a one-time on-prem activation fee and a temporary pilot discount if you commit within 30 days of the pilot finishing.
[04:52] Anita: does Redwood offer any uplift credits if we agree to a longer term? finance will prefer a 24-month with steeper discount.
[04:59] Jordan: longer terms do have meaningful discounts; i'll include an AS-IS 12 and 24 month pricing table.
[05:05] Marta: ok. any open risk that we should flag?
[05:08] Priya: from engineering side: dependency on the HSM integration and network egress are the primary risk. we'll surface required pre-reqs early so infra can prepare. second, model/kernel tuning for your token distribution — we may need a short calibration run to choose quantization and batching knobs.
[05:24] Derek: understood. the calibration run — how intrusive? will it require model restarts or changes to production?
[05:29] Priya: it'll be isolated to the pilot cluster; we won't touch production. we'll run sample payloads and capture the KV cache hit rates and cold-start latency.
[05:36] Jordan: great. recap and next steps — Jordan to send pricing amendment + sample PO and legal language; Priya to send pilot checklist and test plan + security doc links; Derek to share traffic profile and infra notes; Anita to confirm contracting timeline. target dates, folks?
[05:51] Marta: those dates work. and we want the benchmark scheduled for early June, ideally week of the 7th.
[05:57] Jordan: noted. we'll aim to have docs to you by 5/26, pilot plan by 5/24, and coordinate the benchmark scheduling once derek shares infra.
[06:05] Anita: one last procurement q — invoicing cadence ok to be monthly or do you require net 30?
[06:11] Jordan: net 30 is standard but we can discuss invoicing cadence in the amendment.
[06:16] Marta: cool, thanks everyone.
[06:18] Derek: thanks, i'll get the infra doc over.
[06:20] Priya: thanks team, we'll follow up in the notes and drop the security artifacts.
[06:23] Jordan: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
